# Mathematical Puzzles — from tiny examples to rigorous proofs

**Source:** Anany Levitin and Maria Levitin, *Algorithmic Puzzles* (Oxford University Press, 2011). Its source structure has two tutorials and 150 puzzles in three groups: easier (#1–50), medium (#51–110), harder (#111–150), followed by hints and detailed solutions.

The teaching pages here are **original mathematical explanations**, not copies of the book. We keep the puzzle numbers to help you locate the originals. We do **not** create empty pages for the remaining puzzles.

## Before the problems

- [Mathematical symbols, with numbers](symbol-guide.qmd) — ∀, ∃, ∈, ≠, Σ, ∣, ⌈ ⌉, invariants and recurrence notation.
- [Seven problem-solving strategies](strategy-guide.qmd) — representation, invariant, counting, graph, dynamic programming, divide/decrease-and-conquer and lower bounds.
- [Book roadmap](reading-map.qmd) — how this section follows the source book and how to study each difficulty level.

## Tutorial puzzles — learn the basic tools

1. [Magic Square: Why the total must be 15](tutorial-magic-square.qmd) — algebra and symmetry, *Tutorial*, printed p. 4.
2. [Four Queens: Turn attacks into inequalities](tutorial-four-queens.qmd) — constraints and backtracking, *Tutorial*, printed p. 6.
3. [Bridge Crossing: 17 minutes, and why](tutorial-bridge-crossing.qmd) — counterexamples to greedy choice, *Tutorial*, printed p. 17.

## Easier puzzles — establish the language of proof

1. [#1 River Crossing](easy-01-river-crossing.qmd) — state spaces and forbidden states.
2. [#2 Gloves in the Dark](easy-02-glove-selection.qmd) — worst case and the pigeonhole principle.
3. [#3 Right-Triangle Dissection](easy-03-rectangle-dissection.qmd) — construction and induction.
4. [#10 Eight Coins](easy-10-eight-coins.qmd) — information and ternary decisions.
5. [#19 Page Numbers](easy-19-page-numbering.qmd) — counting by digit-length ranges.
6. [#20 Triangle Path](easy-20-maximum-path.qmd) — a recurrence, not exhaustive guessing.
7. [#32 Knockout Tournament](easy-32-tournament.qmd) — counting and logarithms.
8. [#35 Water Jugs](easy-35-water-jugs.qmd) — conservation and shortest-path states.

## Medium puzzles — find hidden patterns

9. [#57 Fibonacci Rabbits](medium-57-rabbits.qmd) — a two-term recurrence.
10. [#79 Locker Doors](medium-79-lockers.qmd) — divisors, parity and perfect squares.
11. [#81 The Celebrity](medium-81-celebrity.qmd) — elimination and verification.
12. [#94 Search a Sorted Table](medium-94-sorted-table.qmd) — eliminate one row or column each step.

## Harder puzzles — prove surprisingly strong results

13. [#121 Two Eggs, 100 Floors](hard-121-two-eggs.qmd) — derive the 14-drop guarantee.
14. [#130 Binary Identification](hard-130-binary-identification.qmd) — use 10 yes/no outcomes to distinguish 1,000 cases.
15. [#141 Josephus Circle](hard-141-josephus.qmd) — recursive structure and a closed form.

## The rule every page must follow

**Question → tiny case → mathematical model → symbols explained → actual numbers → derivation → proof → generalisation → one check.**

Code examples are deliberately optional. Use the [tiny Python verification lab](examples/index.qmd) to test patterns only **after** you can explain them.
